Tipping originally started in England during the 17th century by the aristocratic class. It wasn't until 1840 that it was adopted in the US after the civil war when newly rich Americans visited England. Tipping was largely rejected by Americans until the great depression where it became common place simply because restaurants weren't pulling in enough to afford the staff (patrons at the time hated it). But where the depression left most destitute and dry from prohibition, it left criminals very rich, so the flashy nature of tipping came back. Booze became cheaper and more available so even the common man could step into an underground speakeasy and enjoy a drink and feel rich. After the end of prohibition and the depression as everything else went back to normal... tipping just kinda stuck.

sources:
